q: 1. Public works must be of very good quality, because
options: it is paid in higher rate
users are general public and maintenance is not timely difficulty and costly
explain: But as per book b. Public works serve the general public continuously; poor quality causes costly, delayed maintenance affecting many users, so high quality is essential.

q: 2. The construction of airports is treated as
explain: Airports involve large-scale earthwork, runways, and infrastructure comparable to dams/highways, classifying them as heavy construction.

q: 3. In a line organization
options: responsibility of each individual is fixed
explain: Line organization has strong discipline, quick decisions and fixed responsibility.

q: 4. In a functional organization
options: specialised knowledge and guidance to individual worker is provided
explain: Specialisation gives better quality, less wastage and expert guidance.

q: 5. The salient feature of the organization evolved by F.W. Taylor is
options: separation of planning and design part for field work
explain: Taylor's functional organization separates planning from execution and relies on functional efficiency and strict specifications.

q: 6. The major principle of an organization is
explain: Span of management, unity of command and delegation of authority are all basic principles.

q: 7. The first stage of a construction, is
explain: Construction begins with the initiation of the proposal/idea, before surveys, estimates, or fund allotment occur.

q: 8. Construction team means
explain: A construction team comprises the owner, engineer/architect, and contractor working together to complete the project.

q: 9. The main advantage of line organization, is
explain: Line organization provides clear command, defined responsibilities, and strong discipline - all being its key advantages.

q: 10. Residential buildings are treated as
explain: Residential buildings, being relatively small-scale structures, are classified as light construction.

q: 11. The problem of developing, low cost housing for economically backward people in undeveloped region should be analysed by
explain: Per the answer key, a. Note: option d is a misprint in the book.

q: 12. In PERT technique the critical path has slack equal to
explain: Critical path slack is zero, or negative if the schedule is behind.

q: 13. Cost - benefit studies are essential to
options: assess the total cost of the work
ascertain the relevant escalation in prices
evaluated the viability and worthwhileness of taking up the project
explain: Cost-benefit analysis is primarily conducted to evaluate whether a project is viable and worthwhile to undertake, comparing benefits against costs.

q: 14. The process of inspiring the subordinates to do a work or achieve an objective is called as
explain: Motivation is the specific management function of inspiring subordinates towards achieving objectives.

q: 15. Which of the following is NOT among the principles a project manager must follow in terms of professional responsibility and ethical principles?
options: interacting with the project team in a professional and cooperative manner
explain: Blindly fulfilling a contractor's demands is not an ethical professional responsibility; the manager must act impartially, not favor one party's demands.

q: 16. Clamshell are used to remove loose material from inside
explain: Clamshells dig deep, narrow holes such as cofferdams, pier foundations and manholes.

q: 17. Idlers are
options: used to provide supports for belt conveyor system
explain: Idlers are the rollers that support a conveyor belt.

q: 18. The major principal of an organization is
explain: Span of management, unity of command, and delegation of authority are all fundamental principles of organizational structure.

q: 19. Types of organization used in construction industry is:
explain: Per the answer key, 'effective organization' is listed as the correct type, though line, line-staff, and functional organizations are the more standard classifications used in construction.

q: 20. The final technical authority of a project is
explain: The chief engineer is the final technical authority.

q: 21. The conception of idea for any construction work is
explain: The owner conceives the idea.

q: 22. The types of format in which the records of labors are kept on daily basis for executing works is known as
explain: A muster roll is a specific document used in construction and public works to record the attendance of daily laborers and calculate their wages.

q: 23. Donor funded project are based on
explain: Donor-funded projects consider government priorities, user needs, and economic viability (IRR) - all of these factors.

q: 24. The which one is not concerned with the responsibility of Engineer
explain: While engineers handle technical planning, supervision, and scheduling, core accounting (financial bookkeeping) is typically the responsibility of the accounts department or an accountant.

q: 25. The system of organization introduced by F. W. Taylor is known as
explain: Taylor introduced functional organization.

q: 26. A project is
options: a large dam constructed across a river to earn profit
any job involving many people and large money
a work of major importance involving huge men and investment
an organized team work to achieve a set task within the time limit
explain: A project is formally defined as a temporary endeavor with a specific goal, performed by a team within defined time and resource constraints.

q: 27. Which of the following excavators is most suitable for digging under water?
explain: A clam shell excavator, with its grab-bucket mechanism, is best suited for digging in submerged/underwater conditions.

q: 28. The most critical stage of a construction is construction of
explain: The foundation is the most critical stage because it supports the entire structure; any failure here is difficult and expensive to rectify.

q: 29. Line organization is mostly suitable for
explain: Due to its simplicity and lack of specialized staff, line organization works best for straightforward projects with fewer complexities.

q: 30. The salient feature of functional organization, is
options: each individual maintains functional design part
work is properly planned and distributed
explain: Functional organization emphasizes specialization, where work is divided and managed by experts in specific functional areas.

q: 31. Construction activities at site are directly associated with the management of
explain: Field management integrates control over basic resources: Manpower, Machinery, and Materials (the 3 Ms of construction management).

q: 32. The conception of idea for any construction work is the responsibility of:
explain: but as per book b The owner originates the idea/need for a construction project, initiating the process before engineers or contractors get involved.

q: 33. Motive of private sector for the implementation of the project is to maximize profit while the motive of public sector for the implementation of the project is:
options: Raise the living standard of the people
explain: Public sector projects aim primarily at social welfare - raising the living standard of people - rather than profit maximization like the private sector.

q: 34. Construction activities at site are associated with the management of:
explain: Site construction processes center on organizing resource allocations across labor, construction materials, and heavy machinery.

q: 35. What is the primary goal of project management?
options: To ensure the project is the most innovative
To complete the project on time and within budget
explain: While stakeholder satisfaction is important, the core metric of project management is hitting the 'triple constraint' of time, cost, and scope.

q: 36. Preliminary project report for a road project must contain
options: the detailed estimated cost based on detailed design
the several alternatives of the project that have been considered
the soil survey, traffic survey, concept design and approximate cost
the contract documents for inviting tenders
explain: A preliminary report holds surveys, concept design and an approximate cost.

q: 37. Which of the following is not a goal of project management?
options: Maintaining a happy and well-functioning development team
Delivering the software to the customer at the agreed time
explain: The provided key identifies 'avoiding customer complaints' as the outlier, as management focuses more on delivering defined requirements than reactive complaint management.

q: 38. Construction team in a project consists of
explain: The construction team comprises the owner, engineer/architect, and contractor collectively - all of the above.

q: 39. Policy is
options: a rule or a set of rules never to be violated
a definite route along which one has to proceed
a procedure for preparing the project report
a set of board guidelines stipulated by management
explain: A policy is a set of broad guidelines set by management.

q: 40. Final technical authority of a project lies with
explain: The Chief Engineer holds the final and highest technical authority over a project in the typical hierarchical engineering setup.

q: 41. Duty of obligation to satisfactorily perform a task that one must fulfill and which has a consequent penalty for failure is
explain: That is responsibility.

q: 42. A Work Breakdown Structure numbering system should allow project staff to
options: Identify the level at which individual WBS elements are found
Estimate the costs of WBS elements
explain: A WBS numbering system's primary purpose is to indicate the hierarchical level at which each element resides within the structure.

q: 43. The most crucial time for project risk assessment is
explain: Risk assessment is most crucial during the planning phase, allowing proactive identification and mitigation before execution begins.

q: 44. Major characteristics of project is
options: defined life span with a beginning and end
specific time, cost and performance requirement
explain: A project is characterized by a defined objective, a distinct life span, and specific time/cost/performance requirements - all of the above.
